proposed_status_reason: Base-case cap rate of 7.9% is below the 10% threshold. The $1,242/mo HOA consumes ~48% of gross rent and ~83% of estimated monthly revenue before other expenses. Special assessments remain UNKNOWN (LOW confidence), and the condo-hotel revenue model differs fundamentally from traditional STR—gross rent from a comparable unit may not reflect actual owner net income after hotel management revenue-sharing. Even the optimistic rent scenario ($3,000/mo) yields only ~11.2% cap rate with unresolved assessment and management-agreement uncertainty, insufficient for VIABLE classification.

low_rent_case.notes: Low end of estimated rent range

high_rent_case.notes: High end of estimated rent range; still subject to UNKNOWN assessments and condo-hotel revenue-sharing uncertainty

breakeven_analysis.notes: Breakeven monthly rent of ~$2,850 exceeds base estimate ($2,582) and is near the high end of the estimated range ($3,000). Does not account for potential special assessments or hotel management fee deductions from owner distributions.

risk_factors: Special assessments UNKNOWN — estoppel certificate and HOA financials required per Fla. Stat. §718.116
Condo-hotel revenue model: gross STR rent estimates may not reflect owner net income after hotel management revenue-sharing
Hotel management agreement terms UNKNOWN — controls rental pool participation, personal use limits, and owner distributions
HOA fee ($1,242/mo) is 83% of estimated gross rent and far exceeds the $500/mo scrutiny threshold
Comparable building listings note owners often break even after all-in HOA and hotel management fees
